records.Concise description: A holder-operated 10,000-piece byte-for-byte CryptoPunks inscription collection, broadly recognized as the first coordinated 10k mint completed through Ordinals.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitcoin Punks used an open mint process to place CryptoPunks imagery onto Bitcoin. Its current holder-operated site emphasizes that it was the first 10k PFP collection on Bitcoin, while historical chronology distinguishes it from later original-art 10k collections because the images reproduce CryptoPunks. It remains community-maintained after the mint rather than an actively expanding art supply.
Creators / founders: Open/community mint; current site is holder-operated rather than a conventional founder-led project
records.Launch / history: Minted in February 2023, with inscriptions spanning very early Ordinals numbers and completing a coordinated 10k before original-art 10k peers.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: Bitcoin Punks proved that a coordinated 10,000-item Ordinals mint could be completed early in the protocol’s history and became a reference point for every later 'first 10k' claim.
records.Verification basis: Current holder-operated project site plus historical inscription chronology.
Research notes / uncertainties: Avoid calling it the first original-art 10k; it reproduces CryptoPunks imagery.

records.Concise description: A Ninjalerts Ordinals collection built to demonstrate programmable and upgradeable inscription techniques, including parent-child provenance, recursive resources, and reinscription-based features.
records.Deeper researched summary: Pizza Ninjas pairs collectible pixel-art characters with technical experiments in making inscriptions behave more like programmable applications. Ninjalerts documentation describes parent-child structure, shared/recursive assets, token-gated experiences, and reinscription 'Sat Endpoint' upgrades that can change functionality without discarding provenance. The collection remains a useful reference for application-like Ordinals design.
Creators / founders: Ninjalerts team — project creator; individual creator names not locked from first-party documentation
records.Launch / history: Launched during the 2024 programmable/recursive Ordinals wave and continued with dynamic/holiday traits and application features.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: It is one of the clearer production examples of using Ordinals primitives for more than static media, illustrating composability and upgrade patterns.
Research notes / uncertainties: Individual founder/artist attribution requires a first-party source before public display.

records.Concise description: An Ordinals art project spanning the early Fomojis Genesis/OG works and the later recursive Fomojis 2.0 collection.
records.Deeper researched summary: Fomojis should be represented as one canonical project profile rather than separate OG and 2.0 pages. Early Genesis works were created by Sanj and Swayze; Fomojis 2.0 expanded the concept with generative/recursive techniques. GeneratOrd documentation says the Fomojis team created GeneratOrd and used it for Fomojis 2.0 to reduce on-chain file duplication dramatically by composing shared inscription resources.
records.Launch / history: Fomojis Genesis/OG appeared in early 2023 with inscriptions in the early tens of thousands; Fomojis 2.0 later expanded to roughly two thousand recursive/generative works.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: Fomojis links early inscription culture to the later move toward recursion, shared resources, and more efficient generative collection construction.
records.Verification basis: GeneratOrd documentation plus independent historical coverage and current indexer visibility.
Research notes / uncertainties: Current indexers differ slightly on Fomojis 2.0 indexed count (around 1,998–2,009); avoid a hard supply until reconciled.
Keep Genesis/OG and 2.0 under one canonical profile.

records.Concise description: A recursive/generative Ordinals framework created by the Fomojis team to compose collection assets from shared on-chain inscription resources.
records.Deeper researched summary: GeneratOrd documentation describes a framework for reducing repeated inscription data by referencing shared components recursively, with Fomojis 2.0 as its flagship implementation. The docs remain online and describe the project as alpha/actively developed, but their maintenance language appears older than the August 2026 verification date. MSC should preserve the technical significance while marking current operational status uncertain.
records.Launch / history: Introduced around the Fomojis 2.0 release as a recursive collection-generation framework.
records.Why it matters in the Ordinals ecosystem: It is an early explicit attempt to standardize efficient recursive/generative collection construction on Ordinals.
Important technical or cultural characte: Claimed >90% file-size/data reduction in documented Fomojis use
records.Verification basis: Official documentation remains available; freshness of active development claim not independently confirmed.
Research notes / uncertainties: Current 2026 maintenance/development cadence is not sufficiently verified; retain UNCERTAIN until first-party activity is confirmed.
